# Collateral Acceptance Policy Draft – Needs Improvement

## 1. Overview
The purpose of this draft policy is to outline how the lending desk handles collateral. It loosely aligns with internal credit practices but requires refinement to ensure full regulatory and governance alignment.

## 2. Scope
Applies broadly to lending activities in capital markets. More detail is needed on covered products, counterparties, and regional applicability. Exclusions are not clearly defined and require expansion.

## 3. Policy Requirements
- Collateral should usually be acceptable based on internal rules.
- Valuations are performed, but the methodology and frequency are not clearly stated.
- Haircuts apply, but schedules and exceptions are not listed.
- Legal review happens in most cases, but requirements need clarity.
- Requirements lack measurable criteria and traceability.

## 4. Roles & Responsibilities
Roles are partially defined:
- Lending Desk: Handles onboarding. 
- Credit and Risk: Provide oversight.
Needs: clearer division of authority, escalation rights, and decision-making boundaries.

## 5. Operational Procedures
Some steps are mentioned but lack structure:
- Check collateral.
- Get valuation.
- Review exceptions.
Needs: reference to SOPs, standard workflows, and alignment with enterprise controls.

## 6. Exceptions & Escalations

---

Exceptions occur but the criteria, approval path, and documentation are unclear.

## 7. Compliance, Monitoring & Reporting

Monitoring exists informally. Reporting cadence, evidence standards, and escalation rules need definition.

## 8. Definitions & Interpretation 

A few terms are included but glossary alignment is missing.

## 9. Appendix

Appendix materials need to be added.

The document requires additional work to define monitoring, reporting, and compliance requirements, as well as to develop a comprehensive glossary and appendix materials.

template_fitness_report.narrative: The draft Collateral Acceptance Policy has a fair overall alignment with the policy template, but requires significant refinement to ensure it is comprehensive, measurable, and aligned with relevant enterprise-level controls and processes. The policy's purpose and intent are loosely defined, and the scope lacks sufficient detail on covered products, counterparties, and exclusions. The requirements section has several gaps, including unclear valuation methodologies, haircut schedules, and legal review criteria. Roles, responsibilities, and operational procedures are partially defined but lack structure and alignment with enterprise-wide controls. Exceptions, monitoring, and reporting requirements are also not well-defined. To improve the policy, the organization should focus on strengthening the overview, scope, and requirements sections, clearly delineating roles and responsibilities, documenting standard operational workflows, and establishing robust exception handling, monitoring, and reporting processes. Addressing these gaps will help ensure the policy is comprehensive, measurable, and aligned with the organization's broader governance and control framework.

section_strategy.rationale: The draft Collateral Acceptance Policy has several gaps and areas that require refinement to ensure it is comprehensive, measurable, and aligned with the organization's governance and control framework. The policy lacks clarity in key areas such as collateral valuation, haircut schedules, legal review requirements, roles and responsibilities, operational procedures, exceptions management, and monitoring and reporting.
next_steps: Strengthen the overview section to clearly articulate the purpose, key objectives, and scope of the policy
Provide detailed requirements for collateral valuation, including methodology, frequency, and any exceptions
Document the haircut schedules and define any criteria for deviating from the standard haircuts
Specify the legal review requirements and the conditions under which they are required
Clearly define the roles, responsibilities, and decision-making authorities for all key stakeholders involved in collateral management, and establish escalation paths
Document the standard operational workflows and procedures for collateral management, and ensure alignment with any enterprise-wide controls
Establish the criteria and approval process for exceptions to the collateral policy, and define the requirements for documenting and tracking approved exceptions
Specify the monitoring and reporting requirements, including cadence, key performance indicators, and escalation triggers, and ensure alignment with any enterprise-level frameworks
Ensure all key terms are defined and aligned with any enterprise-level glossaries or definitions
Develop an appendix that includes any relevant references, forms, or supplemental materials

The purpose of this Collateral Acceptance Policy is to establish a framework for the lending desk to manage collateral received from counterparties. The policy applies globally across all relevant regions and legal entities.

## 3. Policy Statement

### 3.1 General Principles
The organization shall accept collateral that meets the following general principles:
- Collateral must be liquid, readily marketable, and of investment-grade quality
- Collateral haircuts shall be applied to account for potential market volatility and liquidation costs
- Collateral valuations shall be performed regularly using industry-standard methodologies
- Legal review and documentation shall be completed for all collateral arrangements

### 3.2 Specific Requirements
- Collateral valuations shall be performed on a [daily/weekly/monthly] basis using [valuation methodology]
- Haircut schedules shall be maintained and applied based on collateral type, credit quality, and market volatility
- Exceptions to standard haircut schedules shall be approved by the Credit and Risk Oversight Committee
- Legal review and documentation, including appropriate security agreements, shall be completed prior to accepting collateral
- All collateral requirements shall be traceable to specific policies, procedures, and internal controls

## 5. Procedures and Controls

### 5.1 Implementation Procedures
The Lending Desk shall follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the acceptance, valuation, and ongoing monitoring of collateral. These procedures shall include, but are not limited to:
- Collateral eligibility checks
- Obtaining independent valuations
- Applying appropriate haircuts
- Completing legal documentation
- Monitoring collateral performance and triggering margin calls as needed

### 5.2 Control Mechanisms
Collateral management processes shall be subject to the organization's enterprise-wide control framework, including regular audits, reconciliations, and management reporting. Any exceptions or deviations from policy shall be documented and escalated as per the defined governance structure.

### 5.3 Reporting Requirements
The Lending Desk shall provide monthly reports to the Collateral Oversight Committee on the composition, valuation, and performance of the collateral portfolio. Significant issues or breaches shall be escalated immediately for review and remediation.

Exceptions to the standard collateral requirements may be granted on a case-by-case basis. Requests for exceptions must be submitted to the Collateral Oversight Committee and will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

- Liquidity and credit quality of the proposed collateral
- Volatility and potential for market value fluctuations
- Availability of alternative collateral options
- Counterparty risk profile and creditworthiness

All exception approvals must be documented, including the rationale, mitigating factors, and any additional collateral haircuts or requirements imposed. The Collateral Oversight Committee shall maintain a record of all approved exceptions for audit and reporting purposes.

## 6. Compliance and Enforcement

### 6.1 Compliance Requirements
The organization shall comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards related to collateral management. This includes, but is not limited to, requirements set forth by the [Relevant Regulatory Bodies].

### 6.2 Monitoring and Review
The Credit and Risk functions shall be responsible for the ongoing monitoring and review of collateral management practices. This shall include:
- Regular audits of collateral eligibility, valuation, and haircut application
- Reconciliation of collateral positions against internal records and external custodian reports
- Periodic review of policy and procedural alignment with regulatory and industry changes

### 6.3 Reporting Requirements
The Lending Desk shall provide monthly reports to the Collateral Oversight Committee on the composition, valuation, and performance of the collateral portfolio. The reports shall include:
- Collateral mix by type, credit rating, and concentration
- Collateral valuation and haircut summaries
- Exceptions, breaches, and escalated issues
Significant issues or breaches shall be escalated immediately for review and remediation.
